lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Hi Omar! I have not seen you since the exam. How did it go?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: She passed the exam because she studied a little every day instead of waiting until the last week.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Sorry, I mean I passed. I studied a little every day this time.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Learning a new language takes time, but it becomes easier once you start using it every day.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: In my opinion, practical skills are just as important as a university degree when you look for a job.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: I agree. By the way, I saw your post yesterday. Do you spend a lot of time online?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: He deleted the app after he noticed that he was spending four hours a day scrolling.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: That was me, actually. I deleted it last month.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: It is difficult to know whether a story online is true, so you should always check the source.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Parents should talk to their children about the risks of the internet instead of simply banning it.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: You are right. Let's talk about something different. Do you recycle at home?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: I try to use public transport whenever I can, because it is better for the environment and cheaper than driving.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: She turns off the lights and unplugs her devices to save energy and lower her electricity bill.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Small changes in our daily habits may not seem important, but together they can make a real difference.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: In my family, we always gather on Fridays for a big lunch, and everyone brings a different dish.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: That sounds lovely. Do you have any special traditions?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: During Ramadan, the streets are decorated with lanterns, and families invite each other to break the fast.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Traditions give us a sense of belonging, especially when we are far away from home.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: It is polite to bring a small gift when you are invited to someone's house, although it is not required.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Speaking of gifts, I need to buy one for my mother. Any ideas?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Try the new shop downtown. I bought this jacket last week, but the zip broke the first time I wore it.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Oh no! Did you complain?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Could I speak to the manager, please? I would like to return this item and get my money back.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: She complained politely, and the company offered her a replacement as well as a small discount.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: I usually compare prices online before I buy anything expensive, because it can save me a lot of money.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Before you pay, check whether the price includes delivery, because some websites add it at the end.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: It is not always worth paying more for a famous brand, since cheaper products are often just as good.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Exactly. Let's go together on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.en: Great idea. I will bring the receipt, just in case!

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.en: Take care, Omar. See you on Saturday!
